17 A hydroelectric power station uses the gravitational potential energy of water to generate
electrical energy.
In one particular power station, the mass of water flowing per unit time is 1.5 × 105
kg s–1. The
water falls through a height of 120 m.
The electrical power generated is 100 MW.
What is the efficiency of the power station?
A
5.6%
B
43%
C
57%
D
68%

hints: Notice the input is water falling: mass per unit time is $1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ through $120 \text{ m}$.
Connect falling mass to input power using gravitational potential loss per second, $(m/t)gh$.
Compare the useful $100 \text{ MW}$ electrical output with your calculated input power in $\text{MW}$ to get useful divided by input.
walkthrough: Identify input energy: water loses gravitational potential energy $mgh$ as it falls $120 \text{ m}$.
Convert to input power using mass per unit time: $P_{in} = (m/t)gh$.
Substitute with units: $P_{in} = (1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1})(9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2})(120 \text{ m})$.
Convert to percentage: about $57\%$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from a power-of-ten error with $1.5 \times 10^5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ or $100 \text{ MW}$.

B.explanation: Too low because the input gravitational power has been overestimated, not equal to about $177 \text{ MW}$.

C.explanation: Input power is about $177 \text{ MW}$ and $100/177 \approx 0.57$, so efficiency is about $57\%$.

D.explanation: Too high because the input power from $mgh$ per second has been underestimated.
